value.text: Personal or family history of malignant hyperthermia.
Conditions predisposing to a hyperkalaemic response (major burns, significant muscle trauma/denervation, certain neuromuscular diseases).
Known pseudocholinesterase deficiency — significantly prolongs its effect.

warnings.value: Malignant hyperthermia is a rare but life-threatening reaction requiring immediate recognition and treatment. Hyperkalaemia in susceptible patients can be severe or fatal. Muscle fasciculations and post-operative muscle pain are common, expected minor effects.

pregnancy.value: Pregnancy category / trimester notes pending sourced publish from authoritative SA-appropriate references.

overdoseSevereSigns.value: Signs of malignant hyperthermia (rapidly rising temperature, muscle rigidity) or severe hyperkalaemia are a medical emergency.

antidoteOrSupportive.value: Dantrolene is the established specific treatment for malignant hyperthermia. There is no direct reversal agent for suxamethonium itself — it wears off through its own metabolism.

clinicalPearls.value: Malignant hyperthermia is one of anaesthesia's most safety-critical, must-always-be-ready-for reactions — screening family history matters before use, and dantrolene must be immediately available wherever a trigger agent is given.

counsellingPoints.value: Not applicable at patient-counselling level — this drug is administered only under monitored anaesthesia/hospital care. Screening for malignant hyperthermia family history before use is the key practice point.

antidoteOrSupportive.value: Sugammadex is a specific, rapid reversal agent for rocuronium (and vecuronium), distinct from the cholinesterase-inhibitor reversal (neostigmine) used for other non-depolarising agents.

clinicalPearls.value: Sugammadex providing rapid, specific reversal for rocuronium — unlike neostigmine's less complete and less predictable reversal — is one of modern anaesthesia's most useful safety advances.
